toegepas.blok: Die ander een dink ook hy is reg

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'By die bal' reads as a location (next to the ball); the sentence refers back to the quarrel over the ball.
toegepas.fout: 'By die bal' reads first as a location (next to the ball) rather than the quarrel about the ball.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal names the situation plainly and ties back to the paragraph's opening 'In 'n rusie'; same children, same event, no new fact.

toegepas.rede_vinder: In an indirect question the verb goes to the end; 'wie doen wat' copies English word order.

toegepas.blok: Wanneer die rusie al begin het
toegepas.voor: Jy kan iets sê soos "Ek voel sleg as jy my goed vat".
toegepas.na: Jy kan byvoorbeeld sê: "Ek voel sleg as jy my goed vat."
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'iets sê soos' calques 'say something like'; 'byvoorbeeld sê:' with a colon introduces the quoted sentence naturally.
toegepas.fout: 'iets sê soos' calques English 'say something like', and the full stop sits outside the quotation.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'byvoorbeeld sê:' introduces the example sentence naturally and still marks it as one possible wording; meaning unchanged.

toegepas.blok: Wanneer dit nie meer 'n rusie is nie
toegepas.voor: lyk na konflik en is eintlik afknouery
toegepas.na: lyk na konflik maar is eintlik afknouery
toegepas.rede_vinder: The sentence states a contrast (looks like one thing, is another), which needs 'maar', not 'en'.
toegepas.fout: 'en' links two halves that stand in contrast (looks like conflict, is actually bullying), which blurs the point.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'maar' makes the existing contrast explicit; the claim is the same, the same things look like conflict and are bullying.

laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Die ander span' clearly means the team that did not score; the proposal only adds words and makes the sentence longer for a Grade 4 reader.

laat_vaar.blok: Die ander een dink ook hy is reg
laat_vaar.na: wanneer jy die volgende keer stry
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Afrikaans says 'die volgende keer'; without the article it is an anglicism ('next time').
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'volgende keer' without the article is ordinary, natural Afrikaans; adding 'die' is a lateral move.
